content:
Maya: FYI support just escalated multiple customers complaining about p99 spikes on Dedicated pool eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3. Started ~09:17 UTC. p95 ~980ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~450ms -> ~3.2s. Error rate up a bit (~1.2%). tagging @eng-runtime @eng-oncall :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260322-78 - Dedicated pool latency spike (eu-west-1)

Kate: Seeing 3 separate tickets from two partners and one internal QA run. All hit the same pool. Customer logs show timeouts at ~10s for some requests, and lots of retry bursts.

Jason: grabbing metrics now. Can someone paste the pool autoscale chart? I want to see scale-up activity + new node startup times.

Linh: chart: cpu utilization and queue length show a sudden jump at 09:16:59 UTC. Autoscaler started scaling at 09:17:05 but new nodes only became Ready at 09:17:34+. Warm-pool eviction events right before the spike.

Dan: looked at node logs — several nodes were terminated by cluster-autoscaler due to binpacking policy ~09:10. That freed GPUs but drained the warm buffer. We also had a deploy at 09:05 that bumped memory usage so the autoscaler tightened.

Jason: so root cause hypothesis: warm-pool was empty (or too small), scale-up initiated but cold start (GPU VM provisioning + container init) added ~20s tail latency for some requests, causing p99 regressions and retries.

Maya: can we confirm cold-start durations? Any logs with instance_wake_time or container_start_ms?

Linh: grep from node-provisioner logs: 
```
[2026-03-22T09:17:06Z] provisioner: allocate vm gpu-a1 id=i-09f.. provisioning_time_ms=18642
[2026-03-22T09:17:30Z] kubelet: pulled image, kv-cache warm=false, container_start_ms=13240
[2026-03-22T09:17:37Z] runtime: model load complete, kv-cache miss=true
```
Cold-start ~18s to 37s depending on image and model size.

Priya: customers are pretty unhappy; two are rate-limited by their apps due to timeouts. Any immediate mitigations we can do?

Jason: immediate mitigations: 1) Temporarily increase warm_pool_size for eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3 to N+2 (we can do this for 30m), 2) Throttle/queue low-priority workloads via route policy, 3) Enable fallback to smaller quantized model variant for new requests until pool stabilizes.

Maya: Kate — can you push a comms note to affected customers that we're investigating and asking them to avoid large batch runs for the next 30m?

Kate: On it. Short message sent to tickets and partners: "We're investigating higher latency in eu-west-1 Dedicated pools. Mitigation steps underway; will update in 15m." :thumbsup:

Linh: I'm preparing a fast revert for the warm pool config. Will run a one-off patch to the autoscaler config: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: PoolConfig
metadata:
  name: eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3
spec:
  warmPoolSize: 4  # bumped from 1
  scaleUpCooldownSec: 20
EOF
```
Patch will take effect in ~10s to the control plane, actual warm nodes will spin up immediately.

Dan: note: spinning up warm nodes will still take ~15s for the underlying VMs. If we need sub-second mitigation we should route traffic to eu-west-1-gpu-pool-1 (warm) or route to hosted fallback.

Maya: Is cross-pool routing easy right now? Can we temporarily route new requests from affected customers to pool-1?

Linh: yes, route policy exists. Quick command to move traffic for partner orgs: 
```
redwood routes update --org partner-acme --pool eu-west-1-gpu-pool-1 --weight 100
```
I'll do this for the most impacted partners after Kate's list.

Jason: Also adding a short-term regen: increase autoscaler aggressive mode flag so it starts extra nodes earlier for the next 15m: 
```
POST /internal/autoscaler/override
{"pool":"eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3", "aggressive":true, "ttl_sec":900}
```
That will pre-provision 2 extra nodes.

oncall-bot: Action logged: Maya assigned to coordinate customer comms; Linh assigned to patch warm pool; Jason assigned to autoscaler override; Dan assigned to check node termination policy.

Maya: I'm going to pause any non-critical deploys to that region. @deploy-bot can you block releases to eu-west-1 for next 30m?

deploy-bot: Release window blocked for eu-west-1 for 30m per request of Maya.

Kate: customers notified. Two asked if we can route to hosted fallback. One has data residency requirements, can't. The other is OK with hosted fallback for short window.

Linh: routing change applied for partner-acme -> pool-1. Autoscaler override posted. Warm-pool patch applied. Monitoring inbound requests for latencies now.

Jason: I'm seeing p99 drop from 3.2s -> 1.0s gradually as new nodes become Ready and routing shifts. Error rate normalizing. Still seeing intermittent 10s timeouts for in-flight retries.

Priya: customers say they're seeing improvement. Still asking about root cause and permanent fix.

Maya: Next steps (owners):
- Linh: follow up with a change to warm_pool default sizing and reduce warm eviction aggressiveness (RFC by EOD).
- Dan: audit cluster-autoscaler termination policy and revert the binpacking change that triggered warm eviction (PR + revert in 2 hours).
- Jason: add telemetry: track cold_start_duration histogram per pool and alert when >5s for >1% of requests (ticket created).
- Kate/Priya: customer comms follow-up and postmortem link.

Linh: quick note: long-term we should add a serving-side fast-failover to smaller model variants for requests that hit a cold container (detect with kv-cache miss + container_start_ms > 10s). I'll draft a design.

Dan: Also propose adding a short-lived cache of warm images (image pre-pull) on nodes targeted for Dedicated pools to shave 5-10s.

Maya: solid. I'll open an incident postmortem after stabilization. For now we keep this thread open until latencies are back to baseline for 30m.

Jason: baseline p95/p99 back to normal at 09:38 UTC. Will monitor.

Priya: customers happy with response so far. One partner wants SLA credit request form. Kate, can you handle?

Kate: Yup, will triage SLA credit requests after postmortem.

Maya: Great work all. Closing immediate actions but keeping follow-ups in issue tracker. :white_check_mark:
